description: Create the implementation plan: implementation-plan.md. This is the phased build plan organized around 'what unblocks what', with clear deliverables and exit criteria per phase.
steps: Create docs/implementation-plan.md covering multiple phases organized by dependency order: Phase 1 (Foundation) - handwritten recursive-descent parser for .do files, AST definition, basic Nim codegen skeleton; Phase 2 (Schema & Database) - schema parsing, SQLite table generation, db.<table>.* query interface codegen, migration diffing and file generation; Phase 3 (HTTP & Routing) - route parsing and registration, ctx object, handler codegen, static file serving from static/ dir; Phase 4 (Templates) - template parser (Pug-style whitespace-significant), inheritance/blocks/partials, expression evaluation and auto-escaping, HTMX embedding; Phase 5 (Auth & Sessions) - auth schema block, session store (SQLite-backed), signed cookies, built-in routes, role system, default-deny enforcement; Phase 6 (Jobs & Scheduler) - job queue table, worker pool, scheduler syntax, retry logic; Phase 7 (CLI) - doot new scaffolding, doot dev with file watching + recompile, error reporting; Phase 8 (dootd) - --prod mode, dashboard UI, deploy flow, GitHub integration, cgroups isolation, host-header routing. Each phase should have clear deliverables, exit criteria, and estimated complexity.
acceptance_criteria: docs/implementation-plan.md exists with clearly phased plan
Phases are ordered by dependency (parser before codegen, schema before migrations, routes before auth)
Each phase has deliverables and exit criteria
Plan references actual technical decisions from the spec (Nim, handwritten parser, SQLite, etc.)
verification: Verify file is non-empty and contains multiple phase sections
findings: Created docs/implementation-plan.md (828 lines). 8 phases organized by dependency order. Each phase includes: overview, key deliverables, dependencies, estimated complexity, exit criteria, and risks/notes. Includes phase summary table, dependency graph, cross-cutting concerns, and decision log.
